Subject: Borealis Health — VPC data paths, air-gapped constraints and next steps

Hi Emma / Carlos — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we dive into SOW/architecture: 

Key context from today:
- Scope: inference-only traffic for clinical NLP workflows (PHI/PII present in prompts).
- Residency requirement: US-only processing and storage; additional region-only access controls for development/staging.
- Preference: private VPC deployment but open to an on-prem air-gapped appliance if required by security.

Open questions we flagged (please confirm):
1) PII scope: is the set limited to direct patient identifiers (name, MRN, SSN) or do you consider structured clinical notes (free text) as regulated PII for this engagement?
2) Retention: target retention windows for inference logs and full audit trails (you mentioned short retention for debug logs). What are your legal/compliance targets?
3) Egress policy: do you require zero public egress (no internet routes from private subnets) or is controlled egress to managed endpoints (S3, KMS) acceptable?

What Redwood can deliver (short answers):
- Private/VPC: we can deploy into a customer-managed VPC with no public IPs on compute instances and optional disabled NAT gateways. VPC endpoints for S3 and KMS supported.
- On-prem / Air-gapped: we offer a Private package that can be run in an air-gapped environment; offline upgrade and packaging is available but requires coordination on OS/kernel versions.
- Logging & retention: configurable. We typically recommend 90 days for token-level inference logs (operational), 365 days for immutable audit trails (access, model versioning) — but we can scope to your legal requirements.

Attachments: I’ve attached a lightweight sketch of the proposed VPC boundary and a short datasheet on Redwood Private (stubbed).

Next steps / owners:
- Borealis: confirm answers to the three questions above + share your internal network diagram showing where inference requests originate (app tier IP ranges) — action: Emma/Carlos by EOD Thu 9/16.
- Redwood (Rishi / Dev): produce a scoped deployment checklist (network ports, required endpoints, KMS integration notes) and an initial SOW draft for Private deployment — action: Rishi/Dev by Mon 9/20.
- Joint: schedule a follow-up technical session to walk the diagram and SOW — propose Tue 9/21 10:00am PT.

If anything above is off, call it out. Otherwise we’ll proceed to draft the checklist and SOW.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Lead
Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers to your open questions: 
1) PII scope: yes — direct identifiers (name, MRN, SSN) plus any free-text that contains patient-identifiable phrases are in-scope. We also treat device IDs and internal patient IDs as sensitive.
2) Retention: legal is pushing for minimal retention. For production we’d like inference logs kept for 30 days and audit trails (access logs, model version tagging) for 1 year. For staging/dev, logs should be short-lived (<7 days).
3) Egress: our security team prefers zero public egress from the inference VPC; all outbound must go through controlled endpoints (S3 via VPC endpoint, KMS via private endpoint). We won’t accept any NAT-driven internet access for inference nodes.

I’m attaching the network diagram we sketched during the call — simplified (borealis_vpc_diagram_v1.png).

We’re happy to aim for Tue 9/21 10:00am PT for the follow-up.

Emma
Director, Cloud Security
Borealis Health

Emma — perfect, thanks for the clarifications. A few follow-ups based on your answers: 

PII handling
- We’ll treat free-text as in-scope and advise redaction options if you want to reduce retained PII exposure (local redaction at the app tier before sending prompts).

Retention (proposed alignment)
- Inference operational logs (token-level): 30 days (configurable, we’ll default to your legal ask).
- Immutable audit trails (access, model versions, admin actions): 365 days (can be exported to your long-term archival S3).
- Staging/dev environments: 7 days.

Egress and network boundary
- Zero public egress is supported. Implementation approach we recommend: private subnets for inference nodes, no Internet Gateway on those subnets, VPC endpoints for S3 and KMS, and a dedicated bastion/jump host in a management subnet for admin access via approved VPN/JIT.
- For KMS: we support customer-managed KMS keys via AWS KMS CMKs and HSM integrations where available; Redwood will not have access to plaintext keys.

On-prem / air-gapped option
- If security requires a physically air-gapped deployment, we can provide an on-prem package. Notes: offline installer, hardware minimums (2x8GPU nodes recommended for HA), and a signed manifest for upgrades. This option increases lead time and will be reflected in the SOW pricing.

Action items (updated):
- Borealis: share the detailed network diagram and a short compliance checklist (how VPN/JIT is provided, internal IP ranges) — owner: Emma/Carlos — due Thu 9/16 EOD.
- Redwood: draft deployment checklist (ports, endpoints, KMS flow), a short runbook for air-gapped upgrades, and an initial SOW with pricing bands for Private vs. Air-gapped appliance — owners: Rishi & Dev — due Mon 9/20.

I’ll attach a short configuration template and a sample IAM policy for KMS access in the follow-up email (Dev will drop the technical note).

Thanks — looking forward to 9/21.

Rishi

Emma / Carlos — a few technical specifics to help your network/security team evaluate quickly: 

Network boundary (recommended minimal set)
- Inference nodes in private subnets (no IGW).
- Interface VPC endpoints for S3 (com.amazonaws.us-west-2.s3), KMS (com.amazonaws.us-west-2.kms) and ECR if you pull images.
- No NAT gateways for inference subnets; management traffic (patching, metrics) can be sent via a controlled proxy in a management subnet that has strict egress controls.
- Security groups: only allow inbound from your app-tier CIDR on TCP 443 to the inference service port. SSH/RDP disabled on inference nodes; admin access via bastion + approved VPN.

Logging & audit
- We push operational logs to a local filesystem and forward to your S3 VPC endpoint. Minimal retention on the node (7 days) then lifecycle to Glacier if needed.
- Audit logs (access, model version changes) are signed and stored for 365 days by default; we can configure KMS-encrypted S3 buckets.

Air-gapped considerations
- Offline installer exported as signed tarball; we need a brief window to validate checksums during install.
- No external telemetry when air-gapped — support will be remote via uploaded bundles (we provide tooling to create a support bundle).

Attachment stubs (technical): redwood_private_config_template.yaml, kms_iam_example.json

I’ll add these artifacts to the SOW package. If you want a sample CloudFormation/VPC template, say the word and I’ll include it.
